definitionEn: to make someone legally or morally obliged to follow an agreement or rule
senseNote: Здесь — «обязывать» (договором, правилами, обещанием); значение «связывать верёвкой» проще.
situation: A contract, law or promise means that people must do certain things and cannot simply change their minds.

examples.text: All employees are [[bound]] by a strict confidentiality agreement, even after they leave the company.
The treaty [[binds]] member states to cut their emissions by half before 2040.
Once you sign the tenancy agreement, you are [[bound]] to pay rent for the full twelve months.

texts: Doctors are [[bound]] by a duty to keep patients' information private.
As a member of the club, you are [[bound]] by its rules.
Neither country felt [[bound]] by the old agreement any longer.

badCollocation.noteRu: Обязан соблюдать договор — be bound by a contract. С with так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: «Юридически обязан соблюдать договор» — be legally bound by it. Tied, connected и linked — калька со «связан», в этом значении не используются.

nuance.text: Both sides are [[bound]] by the terms of the agreement.
nuance.explanationRu: Be bound by — связан условиями, правилами: bound by the terms. Oblige требует продолжения to + глагол: obliged to follow the terms; «obliged by the terms» без него звучит неестественно.

fixIt.text: Once you sign, you are [[connected]] by every clause in the contract, so read it carefully.
fixIt.explanationRu: Обязательства по договору — be bound by. Connected значит «соединён, связан» физически или логически, но не обязательством.

wordFormation.text: The agreement is legally [[binding]], so neither side can simply walk away from it.

reply.context: A friend says: "I want to quit my gym, but they say I have to pay for another six months."
options: That's annoying, but if you signed a contract, you're probably bound by it.
Just bind the contract with some string and throw it in the bin.
One is, regrettably, contractually bound in perpetuity, I fear.
reply.explanationRu: Bound by a contract — «обязан соблюдать договор». Во втором ответе bind понят буквально (связать верёвкой), третий звучит нелепо официально.

rewrite.original: The contract says that both companies must keep the price the same for three years.
rewrite.frame: Under the contract, both companies ____ keep the price the same for three years.
rewrite.explanationRu: Be bound to do something — быть обязанным что-то делать по договору.

definitionEn: an account of a person's life written by someone else
situation: A writer researches someone's life and tells the whole story of it in a book.

examples.text: Her new [[biography]] of the composer draws on hundreds of letters that have never been published.
For the history project, each student had to research and write a short [[biography]] of a famous scientist.
The singer's lawyers are trying to stop an unauthorised [[biography]] from being published.

texts: I'm reading a [[biography]] of the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
The actor's official [[biography]] leaves out his two failed marriages.
Writing a good [[biography]] takes years of research in archives and libraries.

badCollocation.noteRu: Биографический фильм — a biopic или a biographical film. Biography — обычно книга.

collocationTask.prompt: an ___ biography, approved by the family
collocationTask.explanationRu: Биография, одобренная героем или его семьёй, — an authorised biography. Allowed, admitted и enabled так не используются.

nuance.text: The [[biography]] runs to 900 pages and took its author twelve years to write.
nuance.explanationRu: Biography — книга о жизни человека. Biopic — художественный фильм о реальном человеке; у фильма нет страниц.

reverse.text: The [[biopic]] won its lead actor several major awards.
reverse.explanationRu: Главный актёр бывает у фильма, поэтому biopic. Biography — книга.

fixIt.text: The historian spent ten years on her [[autobiography]] of the explorer, based on his letters and diaries.
fixIt.explanationRu: Историк пишет о жизни другого человека, значит это biography. Autobiography человек пишет о себе сам.

wordFormation.text: Her [[biographer]] spent ten years tracking down old friends and former colleagues.

reply.context: A friend asks: "What are you reading at the moment?"
options: My biography! I'm writing it myself, all about my own life.
An elegant tome of biographical erudition, should you wish to know.
A biography of a jazz pianist. The author interviewed over a hundred people who knew him.
reply.explanationRu: Biography — книга о чьей-то жизни, написанная другим человеком. О своей жизни пишут autobiography или memoir, а второй ответ звучит напыщенно.

rewrite.original: A former journalist wrote the story of the singer's life.
rewrite.frame: A former journalist wrote ____ of the singer.
rewrite.explanationRu: История жизни человека, написанная другим, — a biography of someone.

definitionEn: a senior Christian priest who is in charge of the churches in a large area
situation: You talk about the senior church leader who is responsible for all the churches in a region.

examples.text: The [[bishop]] will lead a special service in the cathedral to mark the town's 900th anniversary.
In the Middle Ages, a [[bishop]] often had as much power as a local lord.
Only a [[bishop]] can ordain new priests in the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

texts: The new [[bishop]] was welcomed by crowds outside the cathedral.
She wrote to the [[bishop]] to complain about the closure of the village church.
The [[bishop]] visits every parish in his diocese at least once a year.

badCollocation.noteRu: У небольшого прихода (parish) — priest или vicar. Bishop управляет целой епархией (diocese).

collocationTask.explanationRu: Территория, которой управляет епископ, — diocese (епархия). Parish — небольшой приход со своим священником, а district и county — светские округа.

nuance.text: The [[bishop]] is responsible for more than two hundred churches across the region.
nuance.explanationRu: Bishop — епископ, руководит всеми церквями и священниками епархии. Priest — священник одного прихода; двести церквей ему не подчиняются.

reverse.text: Every Sunday, the village [[priest]] greets his parishioners at the church door.
reverse.explanationRu: У деревенского прихода свой священник — priest. Епископ отвечает за целую епархию, а не за одну деревню.

fixIt.text: As head of the diocese, the [[priest]] has authority over every parish in the region.
fixIt.explanationRu: Глава епархии, которому подчиняются все приходы, — bishop. Priest служит в одном приходе.

definitionEn: very strange, unusual and difficult to explain
situation: Something happens, or someone behaves, in a way so strange that it is almost impossible to explain.

examples.text: In a [[bizarre]] twist, the stolen painting was returned by post with a note saying sorry.
My manager has a [[bizarre]] habit of wearing sunglasses during video calls.
The festival is famous for its [[bizarre]] events, including a race in which runners chase a wheel of cheese downhill.

texts: It's [[bizarre]] that nobody noticed the mistake for three whole years.
He told us a [[bizarre]] story about a parrot that could order pizza.
The film's ending was so [[bizarre]] that half the audience laughed.

badCollocation.noteRu: Непривычные заморские фрукты — exotic fruits. Bizarre — «очень странный, нелепый», это не комплимент.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Bizarre уже значит «очень странный», поэтому его усиливают словами absolutely, utterly, truly. Strongly, much и a lot так с прилагательными не сочетаются.

nuance.text: By a [[bizarre]] coincidence, my new boss turned out to be my old neighbour's twin brother.
nuance.explanationRu: Bizarre — о странных событиях, ситуациях и поступках. Eccentric — о человеке с чудаковатым характером: an eccentric professor. Совпадение не бывает eccentric.

fixIt.text: The police called the robbery [[exotic]]: the thieves took nothing but forty left shoes.
fixIt.explanationRu: Очень странное, необъяснимое событие — bizarre. Exotic значит «экзотический, из далёких стран».

reply.context: A colleague tells you: "The client wants the whole website in purple and orange, with a talking cat on every page."
options: Wow, that's bizarre. Did they say why they want that?
Great, that sounds bizarre. Very elegant and professional.
That is, I daresay, of a most bizarre nature.
reply.explanationRu: Bizarre — «очень странный», и это не похвала. Во втором ответе его путают с «элегантный», третий звучит вычурно для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: one of the flat wide parts that spin round on a fan, propeller or turbine
senseNote: Здесь — «лопасть» (вентилятора, винта, турбины); значение «лезвие» более базовое.
situation: You talk about the parts of a fan, helicopter or wind turbine that spin round very fast.

examples.text: Each of the turbine's three [[blades]] is almost as long as a football pitch.
The ceiling fan was so dusty that grey fluff flew off its [[blades]] when I switched it on.
The helicopter's rotor [[blades]] were still spinning when the paramedics jumped out.

texts: Engineers inspect the turbine [[blades]] for cracks after every storm.
Keep children's fingers away from the [[blades]] of the electric fan.
The boat's propeller [[blades]] were tangled in an old fishing net.

badCollocation.noteRu: Бытовой вентилятор — fan. Ventilator по-английски — аппарат ИВЛ, лопастей у него нет.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Лопасти ветряка или вертолёта — blades. Wings — крылья самолёта или птицы, paddles — вёсла, shovels — лопаты.

nuance.text: The wind turbine's huge [[blades]] turn slowly even in a light breeze.
nuance.explanationRu: У вентилятора, винта и ветряка — blades (лопасти), они вращаются. Wings — крылья самолёта или птицы, которые не вращаются.

reverse.text: Ice on the plane's [[wings]] delayed our flight by two hours.
reverse.explanationRu: Крылья самолёта — wings. Blades — лопасти, которые вращаются.

fixIt.text: The desk fan makes a horrible noise because one of its plastic [[wings]] is cracked.
fixIt.explanationRu: Лопасти вентилятора — blades. Wings — крылья самолёта или птицы.

definitionEn: a sudden strong rush of air, wind or heat
senseNote: Здесь — «порыв, поток (воздуха, жара)»; значение «взрыв» и разговорное have a blast — другие.
situation: You open a door, window or oven and suddenly feel very cold or very hot air hit you.

examples.text: Forecasters warn that an Arctic [[blast]] will bring heavy snow and freezing temperatures this weekend.
Stepping off the plane in Dubai, we were hit by a [[blast]] of hot, dry air.
Can you close the window? There's an icy [[blast]] coming in and I'm freezing.

texts: A [[blast]] of cold air hit us as soon as we left the station.
The hand dryer gives out a powerful [[blast]] of warm air.
Skiers were caught by a sudden [[blast]] of wind near the top of the mountain.

badCollocation.noteRu: Долгая жара — a heatwave. Blast of heat — короткий горячий поток воздуха, например из духовки.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Порыв ветра — a blast (или gust) of wind. Flash — вспышка света, splash — всплеск воды, crash — грохот.

nuance.text: When I opened the oven door, a [[blast]] of heat made me step back.
nuance.explanationRu: Blast — мощный поток воздуха, жара или холода, в том числе из духовки или кондиционера. Gust — короткий порыв ветра на улице; из духовки gust не бывает.

reverse.text: The weather service recorded [[gusts]] of up to 90 kilometres per hour.
reverse.explanationRu: Порывы ветра, скорость которых измеряют, — gusts; это метеорологический термин.

fixIt.text: Every time the front door opens, a [[blow]] of icy wind sweeps through the whole shop.
fixIt.explanationRu: Порыв ледяного ветра — a blast of icy wind. Blow — «удар», калька с «удар ветра» здесь не работает.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Why are you wearing a scarf in the office?"
options: The atmospheric blast in my vicinity is, alas, suboptimal.
My desk is right under the air conditioner, so I get an icy blast all day.
I had a blast of a cold yesterday, so I'm keeping warm.
reply.explanationRu: An icy blast — поток ледяного воздуха из кондиционера. «Blast of a cold» — бессмыслица (простуда — a cold), а первый ответ звучит нелепо официально.

definitionEn: to lose money, customers or staff steadily over a period of time
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «терять (деньги, клиентов)»; прямое значение «кровоточить» проще.
situation: A business keeps losing money or customers month after month and cannot stop the losses.

examples.text: The airline has been [[bleeding]] cash since fuel prices doubled, and it may not survive the winter.
The club has been [[bleeding]] fans after three seasons of dull, defensive football.
Since the supermarket opened next door, our little shop has been [[bleeding]] customers.

texts: The newspaper is [[bleeding]] readers to free news websites.
Experts say the company is [[bleeding]] money and needs a buyer fast.
Our department is [[bleeding]] talent because salaries are so low.

badCollocation.noteRu: Время не bleed: говорят lose time или waste time. Bleed — о деньгах, клиентах, сотрудниках, которые постепенно уходят.

collocationTask.prompt: The business has been ___ money for months.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Постоянно терять деньги — bleed money: the business has been bleeding money. Flow, drip и spill так с деньгами не употребляются.

nuance.text: The magazine has been [[bleeding]] subscribers since it doubled its price.
nuance.explanationRu: Bleed subscribers/money — сам теряешь подписчиков или деньги. Drain — «истощать» что-то: the project drained our budget; у drain подлежащее — причина потерь.

reverse.text: Months of legal fees have [[drained]] our savings.
reverse.explanationRu: Судебные расходы «истощили» сбережения — это drain. Bleed говорят о том, кто сам теряет деньги или людей.

fixIt.text: Since the price rise, the gym has been [[falling]] members every single month.
fixIt.explanationRu: Fall — непереходный глагол, «fall members» сказать нельзя. Постоянно терять клиентов — bleed members.

reply.context: A friend who works in retail says: "Online sales are fine, but our high-street shops lose money every single month."
options: So the shops are bleeding cash? Maybe it's time to close a few.
Oh no, is anyone hurt? Bleeding can be really dangerous.
The shops are, one presumes, fiscally exsanguinating.
reply.explanationRu: Bleed cash — постоянно терять деньги. Во втором ответе bleed понят буквально как кровотечение, третий звучит нелепо книжно.

rewrite.original: The company has been losing a lot of money for two years.
rewrite.frame: The company has been ____ for two years.
rewrite.explanationRu: Постоянно терять деньги — bleed money или bleed cash.

definitionEn: a mixture of different things or qualities that combine well together
senseNote: Акцент на удачном сочетании качеств, стилей или вкусов, а не на простой «смеси».
situation: Two or more styles, flavours or qualities are combined so well that they feel like one thing.

examples.text: The band's sound is an unusual [[blend]] of Irish folk and electronic dance music.
Our house [[blend]] combines beans from three different countries.
Good teachers need a [[blend]] of patience, humour and firmness.

texts: The hotel offers a perfect [[blend]] of old-world charm and modern comfort.
Her novel is a clever [[blend]] of comedy and tragedy.
The perfume is a delicate [[blend]] of rose, vanilla and sandalwood.

collocations: a clever [[blend]] of old and new

badCollocation.noteRu: Blend — удачное, гармоничное сочетание. О неприятностях говорят a combination или a mix of problems.

collocationTask.prompt: a perfect ___ of old and new
collocationTask.explanationRu: Удачное сочетание — a perfect blend of. Blender и mixer — кухонные приборы, stir — «помешивание».

nuance.text: This tea is a special [[blend]] created by our master tea taster.
nuance.explanationRu: О чае, кофе, духах и стилях говорят blend — продуманное, удачное сочетание. Mixture — любая смесь, часто химическая или кулинарная.

reverse.text: Pour the [[mixture]] into a baking tin and bake for forty minutes.
reverse.explanationRu: Тесто или смесь для выпечки — mixture. Blend — удачное сочетание вкусов или стилей, а не масса в миске.

fixIt.text: The film is a clever [[mixing]] of documentary and fiction.
fixIt.explanationRu: Удачное сочетание жанров — a blend (или mix). Mixing — процесс смешивания, а не результат.

wordFormation.text: Put the bananas, milk and honey in the [[blender]] and mix until smooth.

reply.context: A friend asks about a restaurant you went to: "So, was the food Italian or Japanese?"
options: It was a blend. The chef put everything in a blend and pressed a button.
A blend, I would posit, of a most harmonious disposition.
Neither, really. It was a clever blend of both, like sushi with pesto.
reply.explanationRu: Blend — удачное сочетание, здесь двух кухонь. Кухонный прибор — blender, а второй ответ звучит вычурно.

definitionEn: to give someone or somewhere a special talent, quality or advantage (usually passive)
senseNote: Здесь — be blessed with («посчастливилось иметь»); религиозное «благословлять» и «Bless you!» проще.
situation: You say that a person or place is lucky to have a natural gift, good health or beautiful surroundings.

examples.text: The region is [[blessed]] with mild winters, fertile soil and miles of sandy beaches.
She was [[blessed]] with a beautiful voice, but she never took singing lessons.
We were [[blessed]] with perfect sunshine for the whole wedding weekend.

texts: Our team is [[blessed]] with some very talented young players.
The town is [[blessed]] with a beautiful old harbour.
He's [[blessed]] with an amazing memory for faces.

badCollocation.noteRu: Blessed with — только о хорошем. О неприятностях говорят cursed with или plagued by.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Be blessed with — «посчастливилось иметь»: blessed with good health. By, of и in здесь не используются.

nuance.text: We were [[blessed]] with warm sunshine for the whole trip.
nuance.explanationRu: Gifted — «одарённый», о таланте человека. Be blessed with — о любой удаче: погоде, здоровье, природе. С погодой gifted не сочетается.

reverse.text: She's a [[gifted]] pianist who started performing at the age of six.
reverse.explanationRu: Талантливый пианист — gifted pianist. A blessed pianist звучит как «святой, благословенный», а не «талантливый».

fixIt.text: The north of the country is [[rewarded]] with beautiful lakes and ancient forests.
fixIt.explanationRu: Природные богатства не заслужены как награда: посчастливилось иметь — be blessed with. Rewarded значит «вознаграждён» за что-то.

reply.context: A friend shows you photos of her new flat by the sea: "Look at the view from the kitchen!"
options: Wow, you're really blessed with that view. I'm so jealous!
Oh no, you're blessed with that view? I hope you can move soon.
Verily, thy dwelling is blessed with a most splendid vista.
reply.explanationRu: Blessed with — «посчастливилось иметь», это о хорошем. Во втором ответе смысл перевёрнут, третий звучит как старинная проза.

rewrite.original: The country is lucky to have a lot of natural resources.
rewrite.frame: The country ____ a lot of natural resources.

definitionEn: approval or support for a plan, especially from someone with authority
senseNote: Здесь — «одобрение, согласие» (with someone's blessing); значения «благо» и религиозное «благословение» проще.
situation: Before going ahead with a plan, you need the approval of your boss, your parents or the authorities.

examples.text: The merger can only go ahead with the [[blessing]] of the competition authorities.
They got married in secret, without their parents' [[blessing]].
The head teacher gave her [[blessing]] to the students' plan for a vegetable garden.

texts: The city council has given its [[blessing]] to the new cycling routes.
He asked her father for his [[blessing]] before proposing.
The project went ahead with the full [[blessing]] of senior management.

badCollocation.noteRu: Одобрение получают: get или receive someone's blessing. С take так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Одобрить план — give your blessing to it. Put, make и say с blessing не сочетаются.

nuance.text: They were both adults and could marry anyway, but they still wanted her parents' [[blessing]].
nuance.explanationRu: Permission — формальное разрешение, взрослым оно не нужно. Blessing — одобрение и поддержка, которые хочется получить от близких.

reverse.text: You need written [[permission]] from the landlord to keep a pet in the flat.
reverse.explanationRu: Письменное разрешение по правилам — permission. Blessing — моральное одобрение, его не оформляют письменно.

fixIt.text: After months of debate, the mayor finally gave her [[good]] to the new skate park.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Дать добро» — give your blessing (или approval, the go-ahead). Дословное give your good — ошибка.

wordFormation.text: The plan to open a café in the library now has the [[blessing]] of the local council.

reply.context: Your colleague says: "I'd love to work from home on Fridays, but I'm not sure the boss will agree."
options: Ask her for a blessing. Maybe she'll pray for your Fridays.
Petition the superior for her formal blessing forthwith.
Just ask her! She gave her blessing to my flexible hours last month.
reply.explanationRu: Give your blessing — «дать добро», одобрить. В первом ответе blessing понят как церковное благословение, второй звучит слишком официально.

rewrite.original: The council has approved the plan for the new market.
rewrite.frame: The council has given ____ to the plan for the new market.
rewrite.explanationRu: Одобрить план — give your blessing to it.
